newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss to repatriate thousands of Yugoslavs.
newsitem.headline: Swiss to repatriate thousands of Yugoslavs.

text.p: Switzerland will start repatriating around 12,500 Yugoslav citizens without residence permits under an agreement signed with Belgrade on Thursday, the Swiss justice ministry said.

Charitable groups and 13 members of the Berne parliament immediately attacked the plan, which will gradually send back thousands of ethnic Albanians from the Yugoslav province of Kosovo starting in September.
Around 95 percent of the Yugoslavs in Switzerland affected by the accord are from the tense province where ethnic Albanians outnumber Serbs by nine to one, the SDA news agency reported.
Critics of the plan said ethnic Albanians faced human rights abuses in Kosovo.

Serbia revoked Kosovo's autonomy in 1989, claiming its Albanian population wanted to secede and join neighbouring Albania. The Albanians have boycotted Serbian institutions since, and their leaders have openly called for secession.

All Serb-Albanian talks over the past few months to find a solution to the impasse have been deadlocked. In the meantime the province has been rocked over the past year by a wave of violence in which more than 30 people have been killed, despite a heavy Serbian police and army presence.

Swiss President Arnold Koller and Yugoslav Interior Minister Zoran Sokolovic signed the accord. Yugoslavia had until now refused to take back citizens whose asylum requests were rejected in Switzerland.

"In practice this means above all that the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia will take back its own citizens whose residence in Switzerland is unresolved. Voluntary returnees will be taken back without any special formalities," a statement said.
